title: Compact inference operator manifest — draft
content:
Context:
This is a lightweight design sketch for a CompactInferenceOperator CRD/manifest format we can use for fast deployments across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Goal: small, portable, opinionated manifest that captures the runtime constraints we need for efficient scheduling, quick rollouts, and safe fallbacks while minimizing cluster/operator surface area.

High-level goals:
- Single, compact manifest for a model variant that can be applied in all environments (hosted proto, dedicated pool, private cluster).
- Explicit control knobs for cost/latency trade-offs (batching, quant profile, cache policy).
- Built-in safe rollouts: canary percent, rollback triggers, fallback model refs.
- Minimal required fields so on-call/debugging remains simple.

Constraints / design constraints:
- Operators should not assume a full k8s ecosystem in private/on-prem (avoid heavy CRD logic). Keep reconciliation idempotent and tolerant to partial API availability.
- Keep manifest size small: typical payload < 1KB in common cases.
- Backward-compatible: manifest additions should be additive. Provide a "compatVersion" field.
- Secrets (keys/kms) must be referenced via secretRef only — operator never embeds secrets.

Compact CRD sketch (YAML-like for readability):

apiVersion: inference.redwood.ai/v1alpha1
kind: CompactInference
metadata:
  name: search-re-ranker-v2
spec:
  modelRef: "open-models/clm-re-ranker"          # canonical model id in model catalog
  modelVersion: "2025-11-01"                    # immutable artifact tag (s3 path or digest id)
  compatVersion: "v1"                           # operator manifest compatibility
  runtimeHints:                                   # small set of runtime prefs (optional)
    device: "gpu"                                # gpu | cpu | auto
    minGPUs: "0"                                 # 0 = best-effort, otherwise reserved count
    memory: "32Gi"                               # soft scheduling hint
  resources:                                       # soft limits used by scheduler
    cpu: "2000m"
    memory: "32Gi"
    gpu: "1"                                      # numeric or "fractional" (TBD)
  quantProfile: "q4_0"                           # recommended quant, operator can pick compatible container
  batching:                                        # conservative defaults; operator may override
    maxBatchSize: 8
    maxLatencyMs: 120
    warmupPrefetch: true
  cachePolicy:                                     # local prefix/KV caching
    kvTTL: 300                                     # seconds
    prefixWhitelist:                               # simple allowlist for prefix caching
      - "/api/re-rank"
  rollout:                                         # simple rollout config for canary/progressive
    strategy: "progressive"                       # static | canary | progressive
    initialPercent: 5                              # for canary/prog: starting traffic percent
    stepPercent: 10                                # percent increment per step
    stepIntervalSeconds: 300                       # wait time between steps
    healthChecks:                                  # signals used to evaluate each step
      - latency_p95_ms < 200
      - error_rate_5m < 0.01
    fallbackModelRef: "open-models/clm-re-ranker-legacy"  # immediate fallback if metrics breach thresholds
  observability:                                   # passive flags, operator wires up metadata/tags
    tracing: true
    metricsPrefix: "compact.inference.re_ranker"
  secretsRef: "secret:re-ranker-keys"            # operator reads secrets from k8s/vault (opaque to manifest)

Minimal example CR (packed):
{
  "apiVersion":"inference.redwood.ai/v1alpha1",
  "kind":"CompactInference",
  "metadata":{"name":"query-re-rank-v2"},
  "spec":{
    "modelRef":"open-models/clm-re-ranker",
    "modelVersion":"2025-11-01",
    "compatVersion":"v1",
    "runtimeHints":{"device":"gpu"},
    "resources":{"cpu":"2000m","memory":"32Gi","gpu":"1"},
    "batching":{"maxBatchSize":8,"maxLatencyMs":120},
    "cachePolicy":{"kvTTL":300},
    "rollout":{"strategy":"progressive","initialPercent":5,"stepPercent":10},
    "observability":{"tracing":true},
    "secretsRef":"secret:re-ranker-keys"
  }
}

Operator reconciliation notes (pseudo):
- read CompactInference CR -> validate schema (fail early, set status.conditions)
- reconcileModelArtifact(spec.modelRef, spec.modelVersion) -> ensure model is available in model-store (pull or signal staging)
- ensureNodeAffinity(spec.runtimeHints) -> annotate matching nodePools (dedicated pool label, region, etc)
- schedule pods with resources & container image (image selected based on quantProfile & device)
- apply batching/cache config via Env or ConfigMap to runtime container
- wire telemetry tags (metricsPrefix + name) to runtime sidecar or exporter
- implement rollout controller: if strategy == progressive -> shift traffic by patching route (gateway/service mesh) in steps and evaluate healthChecks; on threshold breach -> initiate rollback to fallbackModelRef or previous revision

Failure handling & safety primitives:
- if model artifact missing -> set condition "ArtifactNotFound" and retry with backoff (exponential up to 12h)
- on repeated health-check failures across 2 steps -> automatically set desired replica count=0 and alert on-call + trigger fallbackModelRef patch
- secretRef missing -> do not start, set condition "MissingSecrets" (operator must not expose secrets in logs)

Observability contract (what manifests should provide):
- metricsPrefix: operator emits orchestration metrics for each manifest: compact_reconcile_latency_seconds, compact_rollout_steps_total, compact_fallbacks_total
- tracing tags: manifest.name, modelRef, modelVersion, quantProfile, rollout.strategy

Compact status schema (in CR status) — kept tiny:
- phase: Pending|Reconciling|Active|Degraded|Failed
- observedGeneration: string
- conditions: ["ArtifactReady","Rolling","Healthy","Degraded"] (short list)

ASCII topology diagram (simple):

  [CompactInference CR] ---> operator ---> [ModelStore pull] ---> [NodePool assign] ---> [Pod(s) running runtime] ---> [Service / Gateway]
                                                 |
                                                 +--> [Fallback model artifact] (optional)

Open questions / TODOs:
- quantProfile semantics: string vs explicit object for bit-width, sym/asym, kernelHints. For v1 keep string and map in operator.
- fractional GPU scheduling (TF exclusive vs multi-tenant fractional) — should operator expose "gpuFraction"? for now require integer.
- rollout traffic control primitive: service mesh patch vs operator-crafted ingress. Which is less friction for private deployments?
- schema for healthChecks is currently tiny (string expressions). Need a safe parser / sandbox for evaluation.
- compatibility mapping table for runtime container images vs quantProfile & device combos (maintain in infra repo).

Notes to self / experiments:
- try progressive rollout against dedicated pool (staging) with stepInterval 120s and artificially injected latency to validate rollback behavior.
- unify metricsPrefix naming across hosted/dedicated so SLO alerts can be reused.

Quick API shape checklist (for minimal manifest):
- required: modelRef, modelVersion, resources, secretsRef
- recommended: quantProfile, batching, rollout.strategy
- optional: cachePolicy, runtimeHints, observability

If we like this shape we can prototype operator wiring in infra experiments repo (PR link above). Will need a small reconciler loop + unit test harness that simulates gradual rollout.

Notes: informal — lots of TODOs. This page is a working sketch, not final.

-- Samira
(quick local notes: try to keep manifest < 1KB, minimal string keys, and prefer lookups to embedded objects where possible)
